notes: Good pressure on Server 1, eating Doomscroll to steal Freedom of Information (T5, T7), Stoke the Embers (T9) and Tomorrow's Headline (T14) while the Corp was broke. Window of Opportunity's Doomscroll derez on T12 was wasted because the Corp simply rezzed it again. The T13 Tread Lightly into unrezzed Server 2 ice on 2 credits hit Ping for a pointless tag. Credits stayed thin because so much went to tag removal.

Won by scoring from remotes (Flower Sermon T3, Sericulture T9, Fujii T14), but sat at 0-3 credits all game. It could never rez the R&D ice, so the Runner ran R&D four times a turn and stole Sericulture and Hybrid Release. Project Yagi-Uda went behind a lone Hafrun (T4) and was stolen on T6. Flower Sermon draws repeatedly forced end-of-turn discards (T6, T9, T11), and Hedge Fund sat unplayable for lack of money.

After an early Above the Law steal, the Runner clicked for credits four times a turn from T9 to T26, banking 75 credits with no plan. Its only remote runs were three facechecks into Akhet (T16, T17, T23). It never contested the Divested Trusts (T18, T24) or the Above the Laws (T25, T27) scored out of Servers 3 and 4, and the Corp won on T27.

Sensible game: an early Hedge Fund paid for Ansel 1.0 on R&D, which locked out every steal. Agendas were scored steadily from Hagen-protected Server 2 (Ingatan T6, Melies T9, Ingatan T10). The only weakness was flat clicking for credits on T2 and T4.

Good Tread Lightly steal on T5 and gutsy remote steals on T6/T7, but the T7 run into a second unrezzed Doomscroll with a tag cost 3 cards including The Back. Re-running known Piranhas on R&D (T11, T12) only fed it cards (Sang Kancil, Info Bounty). T10 and T12-T14 were spent on empty Archives runs and clicking for credits while the Corp sat at 0 credits.

On T1 the Corp spent its money rezzing a naked Nico Campaign, which was trashed at once, and left Project Ingatan in an HQ it could not afford to defend. The T2 and T3 agendas in Server 2 (Architect Deployment Test, Megaprix) sat behind ice it could not rez or that was easily broken, and both were stolen. From then on the Corp had 0-5 credits and clicked for credits while the Runner won on T8.

Steady R&D pressure through Funhouse found Oracle Thinktank (T5), Next Big Thing (T6) and Remastered Edition (T13), and the T9 remote run stole Oracle Thinktank. It ate a lot of Funhouse tags without clearing them (T9-T12), which was risky against a tag-punishing Corp. Several draw clicks (T6, T11, T12) caused end-of-turn discards.

The Runner clicked for credits nearly every turn (T3, T4, T8-T14), reaching 47 credits without using them. It let Transport Monopoly (installed T4 behind unrezzed ice with the Corp at 3 credits) and Above the Law (T9-T10, T15-T16) score uncontested. Its only remote run was a T15 facecheck into Descent.

Hybrid Release went into an unprotected Archives and was stolen T6. Longevity Serum and See How They Run sat in an HQ guarded by one Semak-samun that Rising Tide broke, and were stolen T7 and T10. The T8 Mitosis put Lotus Haze naked in a remote, where it was stolen at once. Economy stayed at 0-3 credits for most of the game.

Good fast scores of Hybrid Release (T1) and Regenesis (T4). Against Chastushka's sabotage on T4, the Corp trashed agendas from HQ into an unprotected Archives, giving up Sisyphus Protocol and two Hybrid Releases. It then lived on 0-5 credits, clicking for credits, and won only because the Runner went passive from T10 on.

Efficient scoring out of Ping-protected Server 2: Tomorrow's Headline (T3), two Post-Truth Dividends (T5, T6) and Next Big Thing (T10). Money was very tight (often 0-2 credits) and two end-of-turn discards (T8, T9) wasted cards, but nothing was left exposed.

Won by stealing Above the Law (T2), SDS Drone Deployment (T8) and Transport Monopoly (T10). T1 facechecked both HQ and R&D Akhets with no breaker. T3-T6 were spent passively clicking for credits up to 15 while the Corp was broke and building Server 2. The T7 Raindrops run lost Buzzsaw to Ballista.

The Corp clicked for credits on T2, T4 and T6 while rich, discarding from a full hand, and never put an agenda into its iced Server 1. Next Big Thing (T4) and Embedded Reporting (T9) were stolen from an HQ guarded only by a Ping that Gauss broke for 1. The T5 Oppo Research tags were never followed up.

After stealing Longevity Serum (T7) and Project Yagi-Uda (T15), the Runner spent T9-T13 and T16-T20 clicking for credits, banking 49. It never ran Server 2 while Fujii Asset Retrieval was installed and advanced (T19-T20), so the Corp scored it for the win on T21. Server 3 was also never contested.

Sharp play: the Runner saw the Corp was broke and ran Server 1's three unrezzed ice to steal Fujii (T4) and Longevity Serum (T5). It kept up R&D pressure and found the winning Fujii on T7. Economy (Sure Gamble, two Daily Casts) was well timed.

The naked Nico Campaign (T1) was trashed. The Corp spent T3, T5, T6, T8 and T13 clicking for credits with a full hand while holding agendas, and Project Ingatan was stolen from an HQ guarded only by Hagen (T10). On T7 it paid 6 credits to stack three ice on a Server 1 that never held a card. Its final Megaprix install let the Runner take the last point on T14.

The Runner ran R&D into a known, unbreakable Descent six turns in a row (T2-T8) and made many empty Archives and HQ runs. On T29 it ran HQ twice with no money, letting Ballista trash Banner and Boi-tata, which left it unable to contest the final Transport Monopoly (T31-T32) at 6 points. It also spent T14 and T15 clicking for credits while Transport Monopoly was being advanced.

Sericulture Expansion (T2) and Hybrid Release (T6) were installed behind a single Karuna, which the Runner tanked to steal both. The Corp ran on 0-5 credits, clicked for credits on T3, and repeatedly discarded 1-2 cards at end of turn after AU Co. draws (T4, T7, T8). R&D lay open to the steals on T8 and T9.

Spamming naked Nico and Otto Campaigns into new remotes kept the Runner broke from trashing them, and Server 9 (Drafter, Hagen, Tranquility Home Grid) scored Architect Deployment Test (T13), Melies (T17) and Architect Deployment Test with Seamless Launch (T19). Project Ingatan was stolen from a weakly defended HQ on T4, and the T7 turn of five credit clicks was clumsy.

Strong start with a T1 Next Big Thing steal and later remote steals (Oracle Thinktank T10, Kingmaking and Remastered Edition T13). In between, T5-T9 and T11 were almost all clicks for credits up to 22, applying no pressure.
